title: Fads in Mallworld?
content: Does anyone else's Mallworld have fads that come and go? For me for a little while it's been these small toy electric train sets (looking up a size guide, about N scale), very cheap looking, packaging that has that sort of Chinese bootleg aesthetic. The packaging is usually totally off the wall with barely any mention of what it actually is, and that seems to be part of the appeal. Kind of like how fireworks packaging is in the US where it's extremely random and cornily "extreme", like a bootleg action movie DVD cover or something. These fads are sold in their own weirdly empty stores, that only have different varieties of that one product. Think blank white walls, bare fluorescent lighting, some racks or tables down the middle of the floor sparsely populated with the product, and an empty display case with the cash register on it in a corner. These stores seem to be family run and kind of shady or dangerous, like they're a front for something. The usually husband and wife team running them are quick to anger if you open a box or something. It's never a fad from real life, it's always something that could maybe exist here but doesn't, or not in this particular way. In my mall world everyone knows what the latest one of these products is and it may be like a running gag or side theme to the main "plot" (if present). Another one: Sort of pouches or zippered wallets which I think are something to put your phone in or whatever passes for a phone there. The outer texture feels like a brown paper bag but it's actually a material that doesn't damage like paper, only feels like it, and sort of padded inside. Lighter tan than a real paper bag and it has ironic/silly things printed on it. Like strange phrases in various fonts and pictures of weird looking dogs like pugs. Sort of thing that would be sold in Urban Outfitters around the mid 00s if unbreakable paper existed. If I was nuts I'd suggest that Mallword sometimes feels like Aliexpress or some similar entity created a consumer research sim that invades your dreams and leases out access to makers of random crap. Only maybe it's not really live yet so they're beta testing it with nonsensical placeholder products. Maybe that's what the balloons are doing because the signal is too weak for satellite distances, you get the mallworld if one happens to be within a certain radius while you sleep. Maybe it just comes from one of the zillion wireless transceivers around us. I'm not nuts though so I still think mallworld is your brain trying to transform the internet into a physical construct to work with it in dreams, since we spend so much time there and for many it's as important as real life (work, socialization, etc). If it was the 1800s or something and you lived and worked on a ranch and lived most of your days there I bet you'd spend a lot of time in ranchworld in your dreams. The internet doesn't really look like anything so you get this bizarre glitched out mall-like schizo place where even things that aren't the mall are the mall.
